headline: Highest risk is medium compliance/data-flow ambiguity: Authelia can egress to OIDC/ForwardAuth while the Zoomcamp profile is docs-only and non-runnable, so most pairwise harms are limited but not fully blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. Authelia is non-runnable and exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth, while data-engineering-zoomcamp has no I/O surfaces or runnable agent behavior, so there is no shared channel for one to inject instructions into the other.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the two profiles, injection risk becomes possible.
IF the Zoomcamp profile is wrapped in an agent that parses Authelia output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste channels.
Do not pipe Authelia output into an instruction parser.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared workspace is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and may handle authentication traffic, but the Zoomcamp profile shows no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or sensitive data documented, leakage is not a default pairwise pathway; uncertainty stays low because the interaction is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing secrets, leakage risk increases.
IF Authelia is configured to forward request contents that include sensitive fields, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Review Authelia forwarding rules before enabling shared inputs.
Separate credentials and logs for each system.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with distinct storage volumes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is non-runnable and has no filesystem write capability listed; the Zoomcamp profile also has no write surfaces or concurrency model. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no capability conflict pathway to arbitrate.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory or git state, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable resources, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid placing both under the same writable workspace.
Do not grant shared git or database credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions or forwarded identity data, but the Zoomcamp profile is a course repository with no downstream action-taking authority documented. That makes a cascade possible only if an operator wires Authelia output into a consumer that treats it as authoritative.
conditions: IF the Zoomcamp content is wrapped in an agent that acts on Authelia outputs without verification, cascade risk increases.
IF Authelia outputs are used to trigger emails, commits, or access grants, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Authelia outputs.
Do not auto-ingest Authelia responses into downstream workflows.
Add a verification step before any action-taking consumer.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for downstream consumers.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad egress, while the Zoomcamp profile is docs-only and shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. No concrete residency or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to future deployment choices rather than the default pair.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed through Authelia into a non-compliant deployment, reassess upward.
IF either profile is deployed with conflicting retention or logging policies, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep personal data out of the Zoomcamp materials.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and retention policy if regulated data is introduced.
